text: nikpak is a command-line archiver for the .nik format. It was designed around four ideas: compress better than the established tools, do it faster, protect data with modern cryptography, and run unchanged on Windows, macOS and Linux as a single small executable.
marker: **nikpak** is a command-line archiver for the `.nik` format. It was designed around four ideas: compress better than the established tools, do it faster, protect data with modern cryptography, and run unchanged on Windows, macOS and Linux as a single small executable.

text: Small. Beat RAR 7 on the data people actually archive in bulk. Audio, images and tracker music are detected by content and compressed with specialised lossless codecs; everything else uses a tuned, multi-threaded Zstandard stream.

text: Because nikpak accepts RAR's command syntax (a, x, e, l, t, @listfile, -p, -ep1, -o+, -y, -m), a program that can drive an external rar.exe can drive nikpak.exe. In Total Commander, register the extension nik under Configuration, Packer, Additional packer programs and point the packer and unpacker commands to nikpak.exe. Use -o+ or -y for unattended extraction, because without a console nikpak cannot ask whether to overwrite and will skip existing files instead. Menu names differ between Total Commander versions; consult its built-in help for the exact fields.

text: Hindi, Bengali and Arabic need shaping: letters change form and join, vowel signs move around their consonant, and Arabic runs right to left. egui draws one glyph per character, which would print these languages wrongly, so nikpak orders such texts with the Unicode bidirectional algorithm (unicode-bidi), shapes them with rustybuzz (a Rust port of HarfBuzz), rasterises them with ab_glyph and paints the result as an image (textshape.rs). text: Zstandard combines LZ77 matching with an entropy stage built from Huffman coding and finite-state entropy (FSE). text: A general-purpose compressor sees bytes. It does not know that a WAV file is a waveform whose next sample is predictable from the previous ones, or that neighbouring pixels of a photograph are nearly equal. nikpak's media layer supplies that knowledge: it recognises such files, applies a lossless transform that exposes the redundancy, and lets the compressor (or a dedicated codec) exploit it. This is where nikpak gains most against RAR.

A stored copy can only be opened later by guessing that secret, and quantum computers do not make that fundamentally easier.
